What it is

The Emerald Network is the Bern Convention’s counterpart of Natura 2000: a network of Areas of Special Conservation Interest (ASCIs) that the Convention’s non-EU Parties propose, have assessed, and adopt. The data are owned by the Council of Europe and processed and published by the EEA. The 2025 version, published on 19 May 2026 under CC-BY 4.0, reflects the submissions the Standing Committee adopted in December 2025.

Kosovo is not a Party. Its own biodiversity action plan says so plainly: “Kosovo is not a Party to the Bern Convention, meaning that the Emerald Network has not been developed in the country” (MESP, Action Plan for Biodiversity 2016–2020). The desk review therefore expected this page to be “Not applicable to Kosovo”. The check below shows why that is not quite right.

The EEA copy is open, with a DOI and a map service. The Council of Europe’s own reference portal and viewer returned HTTP 403 to every request from this network, so the Convention’s documents could not be read. The check uses the EEA’s map service, layer “All sites”, in the same way the pipeline reads CORINE Land Cover.

Show how the sites around Kosovo are fetched 
build_error <- NULL
if (!file.exists(cache)) {
  build_error <- tryCatch({
    source("../R/functions.R", local = TRUE)
    ko   <- st_transform(st_union(kosovo_outline()), 3035)
    zone <- st_buffer(ko, 50000)
    sites <- arcgis_query_sf(service, st_bbox(st_transform(zone, 4326)),
                             fields = "SITECODE,SITENAME,COUNTRY_CODE,SITESTATUS,AREAHA,DATE_PROP_ASCI",
                             verbose = FALSE)
    sites <- st_make_valid(sites)
    sites <- sites[lengths(st_intersects(sites, zone)) > 0, ]
    sites$site_ha <- as.numeric(st_area(sites)) / 1e4
    sites$ha_in_kosovo <- as.numeric(vapply(seq_len(nrow(sites)), function(i)
      sum(as.numeric(st_area(st_intersection(st_geometry(sites)[i], ko)))), 0)) / 1e4
    sites$km_to_kosovo <- round(as.numeric(st_distance(sites, ko)) / 1000, 1)
    sites$proposed <- format(as.POSIXct(sites$DATE_PROP_ASCI / 1000,
                                        origin = "1970-01-01", tz = "UTC"), "%Y")
    st_write(st_intersection(sites, zone), cache, delete_dsn = TRUE, quiet = TRUE)
    NULL
  }, error = function(e) conditionMessage(e))
}
have_cache <- file.exists(cache)

The sites within 50 km of Kosovo, cut to that zone, are cached as emerald_near_kosovo.gpkg (420 kB, SHA-256 6d60c560b34df6d0, 2026-09-29).

Kosovo coverage check

The question is whether any Emerald site lies in Kosovo, under which code, and what lies within 50 km of the border.

Site Code Country code Status Proposed Mapped area (ha) Inside Kosovo (ha) Share inside
PROKLETIJE RS0000004 RS Candidate 2006 155,400 127,997 82 %
SAR PLANINA RS0000008 RS Candidate 2006 98,448 97,110 99 %
KOPAONIK RS0000002 RS Candidate 2006 31,389 3,891 12 %
Shar Planina MK0000008 MK Candidate 2008 47,042 1,285 3 %
GRMIJA RS0000028 RS Candidate 2006 1,137 1,137 100 %
Hajla ME000000U ME Candidate 2005 2,265 432 19 %
Plavsko-Gusinjske Prokletije (+Bogicevica) ME000000F ME Candidate 2005 15,752 274 2 %
MIRUSA RS0000032 RS Candidate 2006 258 258 100 %
Protected Landscape of Korabi / Peisazh i Mbrojtur i Korabit AL0000023 AL Candidate 2008 31,359 39 0 %
Mavrovo MK0000007 MK Candidate 2008 73,523 14 0 %

33 Emerald sites lie within 50 km of Kosovo (AL 4, ME 10, MK 6, RS 13). 5 Serbian candidate sites, coded RS, reach inside Kosovo and cover 230,393 ha of it, about 21 per cent of the country. Another 5 sites of Montenegro, Albania and North Macedonia overlap the border by 2,045 ha in all; at a scale of 1:100,000 much of that is the difference between the Emerald outlines and the OpenStreetMap border. No site carries a Kosovo code (XK, XKX, KOS or KV).

The Serbian sites were proposed in 2006, before Kosovo’s declaration of independence, and the Emerald data still file them under Serbia. Mirusha and Gërmia are named after places in Kosovo and lie inside it; the Kosovo parts of Prokletije and Šar Planina take in the western and southern mountains where both national parks lie. This is the “Kosovo merged into RS” pattern: a user who filters the Emerald data by country counts Kosovo ground as Serbian without knowing it, and any statistic computed per country, sufficiency included, may do the same.

What it adds for Natura 2000 in Kosovo

Two things. First, the neighbours’ candidate sites along the border, which a Kosovo proposal should meet rather than stop short of. Second, a warning for every European dataset used in this section: Kosovo’s territory can be present under another country’s code, and a check by code alone would miss it. Emerald boundaries are drawn at 1:100,000, so they serve the site tier only as a first outline (tiers). The Emerald Standard Data Form is structurally close to the Natura 2000 SDF, and its guidance is worth reading when Kosovo designs its own forms; that reading is an open action, since coe.int was blocked.

Caveats and sensitivity

  • Candidate status is the first of the Emerald stages; none of these border sites is adopted.
  • The Serbian sites inside Kosovo date from 2006–2008 and describe data of that time.
  • The status of those sites under the Convention could not be checked, because coe.int was unreachable.

Integration into the pipeline

Low effort. arcgis_query_sf() already exists in R/functions.R; a proposed emerald_sites_near(boundary, radius_km = 50) called after the protected-area step would add the layer, with ha_in_kosovo and COUNTRY_CODE kept so the report can say which sites are filed under another country. pipeline.R is not changed here.

To be completed

## Access

```{r}
#| label: access
#| echo: true
#| code-fold: show
access_table(list(
  try_access("https://www.eea.europa.eu/en/datahub/datahubitem-view/4c4c8086-c940-400b-9064-29063143b2de"),
  try_access("https://doi.org/10.2909/a2a18206-633a-4166-8850-0552661ef25f"),
```

The EEA copy is open, with a DOI and a map service. The Council of Europe's
own reference portal and viewer returned HTTP 403 to every request from this
network, so the Convention's documents could not be read. The check uses the
EEA's map service, layer "All sites", in the same way the pipeline reads
CORINE Land Cover.

```{r}
#| label: build
#| echo: true
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Show how the sites around Kosovo are fetched"
build_error <- NULL
if (!file.exists(cache)) {
  build_error <- tryCatch({
    source("../R/functions.R", local = TRUE)
    ko   <- st_transform(st_union(kosovo_outline()), 3035)
    zone <- st_buffer(ko, 50000)
    sites <- arcgis_query_sf(service, st_bbox(st_transform(zone, 4326)),
                             fields = "SITECODE,SITENAME,COUNTRY_CODE,SITESTATUS,AREAHA,DATE_PROP_ASCI",
                             verbose = FALSE)
    sites <- st_make_valid(sites)
    sites <- sites[lengths(st_intersects(sites, zone)) > 0, ]
    sites$site_ha <- as.numeric(st_area(sites)) / 1e4
    sites$ha_in_kosovo <- as.numeric(vapply(seq_len(nrow(sites)), function(i)
      sum(as.numeric(st_area(st_intersection(st_geometry(sites)[i], ko)))), 0)) / 1e4
    sites$km_to_kosovo <- round(as.numeric(st_distance(sites, ko)) / 1000, 1)
    sites$proposed <- format(as.POSIXct(sites$DATE_PROP_ASCI / 1000,
                                        origin = "1970-01-01", tz = "UTC"), "%Y")
    st_write(st_intersection(sites, zone), cache, delete_dsn = TRUE, quiet = TRUE)

  }, error = function(e) conditionMessage(e))

```

```{r}
#| label: build-outcome
#| output: asis
if (!have_cache) {
  cat("::: {.callout-warning}\n## To be completed\nThe EEA map service did not answer at render time (",
      build_error %||% "no message", "). Re-render when it does.\n:::\n", sep = "")
} else {
  fp <- file_fingerprint(cache)
  cat(sprintf("The sites within 50 km of Kosovo, cut to that zone, are cached as `%s` (%s, SHA-256 `%s`, %s).\n",
              fp$file, fp$size, substr(fp$sha256, 1, 16), fp$downloaded))
}
```

## Kosovo coverage check

The question is whether any Emerald site lies in Kosovo, under which code, and
what lies within 50 km of the border.

```{r}
#| label: check
#| eval: !expr have_cache
s <- st_read(cache, quiet = TRUE)
inside <- s[s$ha_in_kosovo > 1, ]
knitr::kable(
  data.frame(Site = inside$SITENAME, Code = inside$SITECODE,
             `Country code` = inside$COUNTRY_CODE, Status = inside$SITESTATUS,
             `Proposed` = inside$proposed,
             `Mapped area (ha)` = fmt_int(round(inside$site_ha)),
             `Inside Kosovo (ha)` = fmt_int(round(inside$ha_in_kosovo)),
             `Share inside` = sprintf("%.0f %%", 100 * inside$ha_in_kosovo / inside$site_ha),
             check.names = FALSE)[order(-inside$ha_in_kosovo), ],
  align = "lllllrrr", row.names = FALSE)
```

```{r}
#| label: check-text
#| eval: !expr have_cache
#| output: asis
by_cc <- table(s$COUNTRY_CODE)
rs_in <- inside[inside$COUNTRY_CODE == "RS", ]
other <- inside[inside$COUNTRY_CODE != "RS", ]
kosovo_ha <- as.numeric(st_area(st_transform(st_union(kosovo_outline()), 3035))) / 1e4
cat(sprintf(paste(
  "%d Emerald sites lie within 50 km of Kosovo (%s). %d Serbian candidate",
  "sites, coded RS, reach inside Kosovo and cover %s ha of it, about %.0f per",
  "cent of the country. Another %d sites of Montenegro, Albania and North",
  "Macedonia overlap the border by %s ha in all; at a scale of 1:100,000 much",
  "of that is the difference between the Emerald outlines and the",
  "OpenStreetMap border. No site carries a Kosovo code (XK, XKX, KOS or KV)."),
  nrow(s), paste(sprintf("%s %d", names(by_cc), as.integer(by_cc)), collapse = ", "),
  nrow(rs_in), fmt_int(round(sum(rs_in$ha_in_kosovo))),
  100 * sum(rs_in$ha_in_kosovo) / kosovo_ha,
  nrow(other), fmt_int(round(sum(other$ha_in_kosovo)))))
```

The Serbian sites were proposed in 2006, before Kosovo's declaration of
independence, and the Emerald data still file them under Serbia. Mirusha and
Gërmia are named after places in Kosovo and lie inside it; the Kosovo parts
of Prokletije and Šar Planina take in the western and southern mountains
where both national parks lie. This is the "Kosovo merged into RS" pattern: a
user who filters the Emerald data by country counts Kosovo ground as Serbian
without knowing it, and any statistic computed per country, sufficiency
included, may do the same.

```{r}
#| label: map
#| eval: !expr have_cache
source("../R/functions.R", local = TRUE)
ko <- kosovo_outline()
pal <- colorFactor(c("#175CA1", "#D55E00", "#009E73", "#CC79A7"),
                   domain = sort(unique(s$COUNTRY_CODE)))
leaflet(st_transform(s, 4326)) |>
  add_basemaps() |>
  addPolygons(fillColor = ~pal(COUNTRY_CODE), fillOpacity = 0.35, weight = 1,
              color = ~pal(COUNTRY_CODE),
              label = ~sprintf("%s (%s, %s): %s ha inside Kosovo", SITENAME,
                               SITECODE, SITESTATUS, fmt_int(round(ha_in_kosovo)))) |>
  add_boundary_outline(ko) |>
  addLegend(pal = pal, values = ~COUNTRY_CODE, title = "Country code") |>
  addLayersControl(baseGroups = basemap_groups,
                   options = layersControlOptions(collapsed = TRUE))
```
